 The Future of the USPSTF and Evidence-Based Recommendations 
 E. Kaplan and C. Shachar
 In May 2026, two members of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force were fired. Vigilance will be necessary to ensure that the panel continues to adhere to rigorous scientific methods. Read the article. 
 PERSPECTIVE
 AI-Based Translation of Discharge Instructions — Aligning Policy with Practice 
 M.F. Molina, M.C. Rutherford, and E.C. Khoong
 Throughout U.S. health care settings, patients with a preferred language other than English frequently receive oral interpretation services but English-only written instructions. Read the article. 
 PERSPECTIVE
 When Fear Became the Barrier to Care — Lessons of a Clinical Rapid Response during Operation Metro Surge 
 M. Maalimisaq and J. Needle-Suarez
 During Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis, volunteer health care professionals quickly improvised a new system, often without institutional authorization, to continue to care for terrified patients. Read the article. 
 PERSPECTIVE
 The Long Shadow of Bedlam 
 R. Elledge
 A dying patient in a state psychiatric hospital has no access to a DNR order that would make the process as peaceful as possible — as the notorious Bedlam casts a shadow over mental health care to this day. Read the article.

 Atorvastatin, Cardiovascular Events, and Disability-free Survival in Older Adults 
 S. Zoungas and Others
 In older adults without cardiovascular disease, treatment with atorvastatin led to a lower risk of major cardiovascular events than placebo at a median of 5.9 years but did not result in longer disability-free survival. Read the article.

 Telehealth Access to Mifepristone — Evaluating Reproductive-Coercion Arguments 
 E. Tobin-Tyler and G. Chalker
 Antiabortion advocates have asserted that mifepristone must be prescribed in person to prevent reproductive coercion, specifically forced abortions. But this argument targets the wrong culprit. Read the article.
